title: Broadcom Gathers $60B to Fund AI Chips for Anthropic and Peers

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
A group of Wall Street lenders is arranging new credit facilities to support the purchase of high-end computing hardware for firms building large language models. Broadcom is coordinating a la syndicate to raise $60 billion for this pool of financing, which will benefit Anthropic and other AI developers, according to sources. This expansion follows a separate $42 billion convertible loan provided by Broadcom to help Anthropic fund a $125.2 billion, five year lease for TPU chips, an arrangement that potentially makes Anthropic Broadcom's largest compute customer by 2027.

The capital influx arrives as Anthropic prepares for an initial public offering, with a trading debut targeted before Nov. 26 and formal marketing scheduled for the week of Nov. 9. Investors estimate a fair valuation for the AI lab between $1.8 trillion and $2 trillion, though some analysts suggest $1.5 trillion. An IPO prospectus reveals Anthropic has total infrastructure obligations of $518 billion over the next decade, 80% of which are noncancelable, including up to $84.5 billion in Nvidia compute via SpaceX by 2029.

selectedTweets.text:
Broadcom $AVGO has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42B in financing tied to its AI infrastructure buildout.

The facility could cover roughly one-third of Anthropic’s $125.2B five-year TPU compute commitment, and the debt may be convertible into Anthropic shares.

Anthropic is also expected to become Broadcom’s largest compute customer in 2027.

The filing says Broadcom’s combined role as hardware supplier and financing partner creates potential conflicts around pricing and access to compute.

Source: Anthropic’s IPO prospectus seen by Reuters

Anthropic is reportedly targeting an IPO before Thanksgiving, with formal marketing potentially starting as soon as the week of Nov. 9 and trading beginning before the Nov. 26 holiday.

The company is still expected to go public by year-end, with prospective investors said to see a fair valuation around $1.8T–$2T.

Anthropic is also expected to match or exceed the size of SpaceX’s IPO, while OpenAI has postponed its own listing plans.

The timeline could still shift.

Source: Bloomberg

selectedTweets.text:
Broadcom has agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B, and Anthropic would spend that money renting AI chips that Broadcom helps build with Google. 

The loan could cover about 1/3 of Anthropic's $125.2B, 5-year chip lease, and the debt could later convert into Anthropic shares.

Broadcom can bring in a financing partner, and the debt could convert into Anthropic shares, though Anthropic expects no note sales before its IPO.

Much of that money would flow back to Broadcom, which expects Anthropic to become its largest compute customer in 2027.

Like Nvidia, Broadcom is using its balance sheet to sell chips, having already backstopped senior debt in a $35B Apollo-Blackstone vehicle that leases chips to Anthropic.

Anthropic ofcourse warned that Broadcom's dual role as supplier and lender creates "potential conflicts of interest" that could affect its access to compute.
